title: LaplacianFormer:Rethinking Linear Attention with Laplacian Kernel
claim: Distance distributions between queries and keys differ sharply by metric: squared Euclidean has heavy tails while L1 is concentrated, motivating a different kernel.
layout: 3 side-by-side histogram panels, left-to-right, captioned (a) DeiT, PVT, Swin
description: The figure is a row of overlaid histogram panels, one for each backbone: DeiT, PVT and Swin. The crop shows the full DeiT panel and part of the PVT panel. Each panel is titled 'Attention Q-K Vector Distance Distribution'. The x-axis is distance value and the y-axis is density. Blue bars show the L1 distance and red bars show the squared L2 distance, as the legend in the top right says. In the DeiT panel the blue L1 histogram forms a tall, narrow peak near 50. The red L2² histogram is flatter and has a long right tail out to about 300. The overlap appears purple. A large '(a) DeiT' label sits below the panel. The eye goes first to the tall blue peak against the spread-out red distribution.
caption: Distributions of $\ell_1$ and $\ell_2^2$ Q-K distances in DeiT, PVT, and Swin Transformers.
abstract: The quadratic complexity of softmax attention presents a major obstacle for scaling Transformers to high-resolution vision tasks. Existing linear attention variants often replace the softmax with Gaussian kernels to reduce complexity, but such approximations lack theoretical grounding and tend to oversuppress mid-range token interactions. We propose LaplacianFormer, a Transformer variant that employs a Laplacian kernel as a principled alternative to softmax, motivated by empirical observations and theoretical analysis. To address expressiveness degradation under low-rank approximations, we introduce a provably injective feature map that retains fine-grained token information. For efficient computation, we adopt a NystrÃ¶m approximation of the kernel matrix and solve the resulting system using Newton--Schulz iteration, avoiding costly matrix inversion and SVD. We further develop custom CUDA implementations for both the kernel and solver, enabling high-throughput forward and backward passes suitable for edge deployment. Experiments on ImageNet show that LaplacianFormer achieves strong performance-efficiency trade-offs while improving attention expressiveness.
